cf.title: Let an ordering index scan hand its ORDER BY value to the target list

input.subject: Let an ordering index scan hand its ORDER BY value to the target list

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support: message #3 agrees the double evaluation should be fixed, and the series answers the main complaints recorded in [P2]. Three design points are still open. maintenance-fit-1: 0007 and 0008 add a path property that nothing checks. standards-compat-1: extension opclasses cannot opt in. prior-attempts-1: nobody working on amgetbatch has said the series fits it. demand-1 and prior-attempts-2 put the cost of 0007-0008 in question. Nothing that survived is fatal.

brief.title: Reuse index-computed ORDER BY and expression values instead of re-evaluating them
brief.problem: When a kNN index scan orders by an operator and the query also selects that expression, the executor evaluates it again per row (a third time on recheck). The planner also charges index scans and index-only scans for expressions they read from the index, so it can pick Seq Scan + Sort. This costs users of expensive distance or ranking functions and expression indexes.
brief.proposed_design: A new optional index AM callback says whether an opclass's non-rechecked ORDER BY values equal the operator's result; when it does, setrefs replaces a matching top-level target entry with a reference to the scan's value. Later patches stop charging for such values, give index paths their own PathTarget, and carry the values up through joins, Appends, Gather and outer joins. Patch 0001 separately makes the point-to-box distance exact.
user_visible_surface: New IndexAmRoutine callback amcanreturnorderby(opfamily, opcintype, orderbyop), NULL by default.
New EXPLAIN VERBOSE line "Order By Values Used: N" on index scans; Output lines gain extra parentheses.
GiST point_ops and box_ops, SP-GiST quad_point_ops, kd_point_ops and box_ops answer yes.
<->(point, box), <->(box, point) and ##(point, box) results change in edge cases; SP-GiST box distance now errors on overflow and returns NaN for NaN input.
Planner plan choices change for queries with costly ORDER BY or index expressions; new add_path_precheck_extras() and add_partial_path_precheck_extras() functions.
author_claims: Query output does not depend on plan choice, because a qualifying opclass promises its value equals the operator's result.
Expression-index kNN queries ran about 88-94% faster; point kNN changes are within noise.
HammerDB mixes with targeted queries gained up to +196% throughput; TPROC-C and TPROC-H plans and timings are unchanged.
Carrying values through joins adds up to +49% planning time and more planner memory at eleven rels, only when an expression costs more than 10 times cpu_operator_cost.
An extension-side workaround using a backend global breaks with nested ordering scans; the core version has no such hazard.
brief.thread_state: Matthias van de Meent agreed the double evaluation should be fixed and shaped the per-opclass callback; Oleg Bartunov reported a 1.7-2.2x speedup with a ranked GIN prototype. No one has reviewed v13 or the planner patches 0003-0008, and the entry has no reviewer.
unclear: No committer or planner expert has commented on the PathTarget and add_path() changes in 0006-0008.
The thread does not say whether the series should wait for the amgetbatch index scan rework that Tom suggested in 2023.
Only float4 and float8 ORDER BY values qualify; the thread does not say how other types would be supported.
Matching uses equal() on top-level entries, so semantically equal but differently built expressions are missed.
Whether the planning time and memory cost at deep joins is acceptable is still an open question from the author.

prior_attempts.title: Avoid computing ORDER BY junk columns unnecessarily
prior_attempts.quote: My basic complaint is that this is a band-aid that only touches things at a surface level, whereas I think we need a much deeper set of changes in order to have a plausible solution.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane found that the patch changes only the final top-level targetlist, so lower plan nodes still compute the expensive expression and cost estimates do not reflect the saving. He also thought the resjunk enum change was invasive and suggested waiting for the work on unifying index scans and index-only scans. Richard Guo found Assert failures with postgres_fdw and with FOR UPDATE queries, and CFbot later reported test failures with no new version posted.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 removed junk columns only in the final targetlist and changed resjunk to an enum. This series leaves resjunk alone, fixes costing (0003, 0005) and carries values below joins (0004, 0007). The advice to wait for index scan unification is still open.

prior_attempts.title: Index Only Scan for index expressions
prior_attempts.quote: Based on this report, this patch appears to have bugs that would preclude committing it, so I'm marking it "Returned with Feedback" for this CommitFest, which is due to end shortly.
prior_attempts.reason: Testing of the sixth patch version by Vladimir Sitnikov found an error ("variable not found in subplan target list") when queries access non-indexed columns alongside an expression index. Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback because these bugs precluded committing it before the CommitFest ended, while inviting resubmission and saying the effort was good.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 added index-only scan matching for expression columns and was returned because of bugs. This series keeps the existing matching and changes costing and path targets (0005, 0006).

prior_attempts.title: Improve use of expression indexes for ORDER BY
prior_attempts.what_is_different: The row lists a similar goal as not worth doing but records no reason. This series brings measurements and a ranked GIN test from message #16.

objections.title: Join-level value carrying adds a new path property with no planner owner
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new join strategy, Append variant or path node and does not propagate or compare the extra values. Nothing fails. The value is recomputed or the cost model credits a value setrefs does not deliver, and users find a slower plan only after upgrading.
objections.argument: Patches 0007 and 0008 make extra values a third axis of path comparison next to cost and pathkeys. They touch add_path(), the new precheck_extras functions, Gather, Material, Memoize, three Append builders and outer-join nullingrels matching. Each future path type has to know about it, and the only check is that the cost side and setrefs agree. No planner committer has commented on 0006-0008, and the entry has no reviewer.
objections.author_must_show: Which committer familiar with add_path() and setrefs.c will own the extra-values property, and what would fail loudly when a new path type ignores it?

critic.reasoning: 0007 and 0008 make extra values a property that add_path(), the prechecks, joins, Gather and Appends must each handle. The material names nothing that fails when a new path type ignores it, and nobody has reviewed these patches.

objections.title: Out-of-core GiST and SP-GiST opclasses have no way to opt in
objections.failure_scenario: An extension maintainer ships a GiST opclass whose distance function already returns the operator's exact float8 result, for example a trigram or btree_gist-style distance. With this series the scan still computes the operator again, because only the core point and box opclasses answer yes. Each new opclass needs a core patch and a major release.
objections.argument: The 0002 commit message says GiST answers yes for point_ops and box_ops and that "any out-of-core opclass" defaults to no. Message #1 names btree_gist and pg_trgm among the beneficiaries, and Matthias in message #3 framed this as a per-opclass property. Postgres records opclass capabilities through support functions or opclass properties that an extension can declare. A list of core opclasses inside the AM departs from that practice, and the proposal does not explain why.
objections.author_must_show: How does an extension's GiST or SP-GiST opclass declare that its distances are exact, without a change to core?

critic.reasoning: The 0002 commit message says any out-of-core opclass defaults to no, and the callback belongs to the AM. An extension GiST or SP-GiST opclass has no way to answer yes, though message #1 names pg_trgm and btree_gist as cases.

objections.title: Earlier advice to wait for index scan unification is not yet settled
objections.failure_scenario: The amgetbatch rework restructures nodeIndexscan.c and how index scans and index-only scans return values. Whoever commits it must then rework two separate mechanisms from this series: the INNER_VAR slot for ORDER BY values and the index-only scan extra-values path. Neither the amgetbatch authors nor a planner committer has said whether that is a mechanical rebase.
objections.argument: In [P2], waiting for the index scan and index-only scan unification was part of the 2023 feedback, and message #9 confirms this. The series still adds two value paths and a new IndexAmRoutine callback that the unification would likely touch. Message #9 answers that rebasing 0001 is mechanical because the series avoids the AM interface, but 0002 adds amcanreturnorderby to amapi.h. Nobody working on amgetbatch has replied in the thread.
objections.author_must_show: Does someone working on amgetbatch agree that the virtual-slot ORDER BY plumbing and the index-only scan extra values fit the unified scan design?

precedents.title: Avoid computing ORDER BY junk columns unnecessarily

critic.reasoning: Message #9 answers this only with the author's own view, and message #11 corrects it: the series does add an index AM callback. Nobody working on amgetbatch has replied in the thread.

objections.title: Join-level carrying depends on procost, which is mostly a default
objections.failure_scenario: A user has an expression index on a cheap plpgsql or SQL function left at the default COST 100, which passes the 10 times cpu_operator_cost gate. Their eleven-way join then plans about 49% slower and uses more planner memory with no execution gain. Meanwhile an expensive C distance function at COST 1 gets no credit, and the plan stays as before.
objections.argument: [P8] was reverted because "relying on procost to distinguish the relative costs" means little when most functions keep default costs. 0007 uses procost to decide whether a value is carried at all, and the overhead in message #20 is real. Message #7 says a costly function at default COST may not flip its plan, and message #16 says a static COST is not enough. Message #20 points to SupportRequestCost, but few functions have one.
objections.author_must_show: How many real expression-index and kNN functions carry an accurate procost, and what bounds planning cost when the gate passes for a function whose cost is wrongly declared?

precedents.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".

critic.reasoning: A default COST 100 function passes the gate, and message #20 measures +49% planning time at eleven rels. The gate copies the make_sort_input_target() test, which lowers the weight, but the thread shows no bound for a wrongly declared cost.

objections.title: Join, outer-join and parallel carrying (0007, 0008) lacks shown user demand
objections.failure_scenario: A committer takes 0007 and 0008, which add new add_path() dominance rules, extras-aware prechecks and nullingrels relabeling for outer joins, Gather and ordered Appends. Every later planner patch that touches path comparison or join targets must then keep these rules correct, while no reported workload is known to need them.
objections.argument: The demand in the thread covers single-scan kNN reuse: message #3 agrees the double evaluation should be fixed, and message #16 reports a ranked GIN prototype gaining 1.7-2.2x. The join and outer-join cases rest only on constructed queries and on HammerDB mixes built with COST 5000 plpgsql functions (messages #13, #15). Message #14 adds 0008 with the words "I cared", and message #13 asks whether planning cost up to +49% at eleven rels is acceptable without a user case to weigh it against. The planner code is maintained by everyone, but the gain goes to a group the material does not identify.
objections.author_must_show: Which real queries, from users or from extensions such as ranked GIN, put an expensive index expression below a join, an outer join or a Gather today?

critic.reasoning: Tom's 2023 feedback, quoted in message #9 and recorded in [P2], asked for handling below the top plan level, which supports 0004 and the join part of 0007. For outer joins, Gather and ordered Appends the thread shows only constructed queries.

other_surviving.title: Existing plans flip based on declared function COST alone
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user marked a function COST 1000 to push its evaluation past a sort. After upgrade, queries over an index on that function switch from Sort to a kNN or index-only plan. Those plans can touch about 100 times more buffers, and on a cold cache the query runs slower. The user finds out from production latency after the upgrade.
other_surviving.argument: The series makes per-path plan choice depend on procost, while before this cost was charged to all paths equally. Message #12 reports a crossover case where the kNN plan touched about 200k buffers against 1.7k for Sort, and all timings were taken prewarmed. The revert recorded in [P8] said cost-based choices that rest on procost are fragile because procost is rarely accurate. That reason applies here, although these are user functions and the planner has no other cost source.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How do plan flips behave on cold caches for misdeclared COST values, and what can a user do to get the old plan back?

precedents.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".

critic.reasoning: All timings in the thread are prewarmed, and message #12 shows a crossover where the kNN plan reads about 100 times more buffers. [P8] must not be used as support: the series removes a charge the scan does not pay and adds no new estimate.

other_surviving.title: Stored generated columns already avoid re-evaluating expensive indexed expressions
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user with a costly immutable function adds `expensive(i)` as a stored generated column and indexes that column, and gets most of the gain on current releases without 0005-0008. The planner patches would still bring up to +49% planning time and about 1.5 times the planner memory at eleven rels for queries that use expression indexes.
other_surviving.argument: The largest wins (88-94% in message #12, about 20 times in 0006, -97% in message #13) come from not re-projecting the indexed expression, as message #10 notes. A stored generated column stores the value in the heap, so every plan reads it and the existing plain-column planner logic applies. The thread does not compare the series against this idiom. The cost is extra heap storage and write work, which is less convenient but still works, while the series adds join and Append planner state that every later planner patch must keep correct.
other_surviving.author_must_show: For the expression-index cases in 0005-0008, what does a stored generated column fail to give users, apart from extra heap storage?

critic.reasoning: A stored generated column gives every plan the value for the expression-index cases in 0005-0008, at the cost of heap storage and write work. The thread does not compare the series with it or show that this cost is a common obstacle.

refuted.title: Point-to-box operator results change for existing data after upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A user has a stored generated column, a materialized view or a btree expression index on b <-> p or ##(p, b). After pg_upgrade the operator returns the corrected values, but the stored values and index keys still hold the old ones. Index lookups can then disagree with a sequential scan, and nothing reports it until the user runs REINDEX or REFRESH.
refuted.argument: Patch 0001 changes immutable operator results in edge cases and changes ## to return a different corner for infinite inputs. It also makes SP-GiST box kNN scans raise an error on overflow where they returned a result before. Message #20 presents these as corrections, which is a fair reading, but the material says nothing about release notes, REINDEX advice or queries that start to fail. A committer would likely ask for that before the change goes in.
refuted.author_must_show: What will the release notes tell users who stored or indexed these operator results, and which queries could start raising errors after upgrade?

critic.reasoning: The 0001 commit message lists each changed result and the new SP-GiST overflow error, which GiST and the operator already raise. Correcting an immutable function in a major release is existing practice, and release notes are written from the commit message.

refuted.title: The 10x cpu_operator_cost gate admits every default-cost SQL or PL/pgSQL function
refuted.failure_scenario: A user has an expression index on a cheap PL/pgSQL or SQL function left at the default COST 100 and runs ten-table joins that select it. After upgrade, planning takes about 49% longer and uses about 40% more planner memory, with no gain at execution time.
refuted.argument: Message #13 and message #20 present the overhead as paid only for expressions worth carrying. A non-C function defaults to COST 100, which is 40 times cpu_operator_cost, so the gate tests the declared cost and not the real one. Message #7 already notes that a declared COST does not follow the real cost. [P8] was reverted partly because procost labels do not tell functions apart in practice.
refuted.author_must_show: What does planning time look like for many-way joins over expression indexes on cheap default-cost user functions, and should the gate depend on something other than procost?

precedents.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-2. It also misstates COST 100 as 40 times cpu_operator_cost; procost is in units of cpu_operator_cost, so it is 100 times.

refuted.title: Index AM callback shaped around float8 delivery and INNER_VAR reuse
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension AM author implements amcanreturnorderby for a non-float score type and gets no substitution. Later, the amgetbatch rework or a second scan-level value source needs the scan's INNER_VAR slot. Then the callback and the executor plumbing have to change after extensions depend on them.
refuted.argument: The callback only matters for float4 and float8, because index_store_float8_orderby_distances() is the only delivery path (message #22). It also uses INNER_VAR inside a scan node, which no other scan does. The unclear points note that the thread does not settle whether this should wait for the index scan rework Tom suggested. Once released, the IndexAmRoutine field is an extension API the project must keep.
refuted.author_must_show: How would non-float ORDER BY values be supported without changing the callback, and how does the INNER_VAR slot fit the planned amgetbatch scan interface?

critic.reasoning: The callback takes (opfamily, opcintype, orderbyop) and names no result type; the float4/float8 limit sits in setrefs.c and the executor, so lifting it leaves the callback unchanged. The INNER_VAR slot is executor-internal, and the amgetbatch part duplicates prior-attempts-1.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: 0001 changes <-> and ## results for point and box, so stored values and expression indexes built on them can hold old results after pg_upgrade.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0002 adds the IndexAmRoutine callback amcanreturnorderby; 0007 adds add_path_precheck_extras() and new path and plan node fields.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: 0003-0008 change costing, give index paths their own PathTarget and add a dominance rule to add_path().

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0001 changes the results of immutable operators and adds an overflow error in SP-GiST box distance, so it cannot be backpatched.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Extra values become a path property that joins, Gather, Appends, the prechecks and setrefs.c must all keep in agreement.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: 0007 adds up to +49% planning time and more planner memory at eleven rels when an expression passes the cost gate.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: For the expression-index cases in 0005-0008, a stored generated column already gives every plan the value.

questions: Which real queries, from users or extensions, put an expensive index expression below an outer join, a Gather or an ordered Append today?
What fails loudly when a new path type or join strategy does not propagate or compare the extra values added in 0007 and 0008?
How does an extension's GiST or SP-GiST opclass declare that its distances are exact, without a change to core?
Does someone working on amgetbatch agree that the INNER_VAR slot for ORDER BY values and the index-only scan extra values fit the unified scan design?
What bounds planning time when a cheap function left at the default COST 100 passes the 10 times cpu_operator_cost gate in a many-way join?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows add_path(), PathTarget handling and setrefs.c for 0003-0008, and someone who knows the index AM interface and the amgetbatch work for 0002.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new IndexAmRoutine callback that extensions will depend on, and for a new path comparison rule that every later planner patch must respect. Both last for as long as the planner and the AM API exist.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted thirteen versions in about six weeks and answered review comments in the thread, so follow-up looks likely.

priority.reason: Users of expensive kNN operators and expression indexes gain, and 0001-0003 look separable and lower-risk. The eight-patch series changes add_path(), join targets and setrefs.c, and no planner committer has reviewed 0003-0008.

provisional_note: Without the code, the agreement between path_target_cost() and the setrefs.c rewrite cannot be checked. The same holds for the outer-join nullingrels matching in 0008 and the EvalPlanQual and reorder-queue value handling in 0002.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid computing ORDER BY junk columns unnecessarily
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a projection at the end of grouping_planner() that removes junk columns added only for ORDER BY or GROUP BY, so expensive sort expressions satisfied by an index are not computed. To mark which junk columns can be removed, it turns the resjunk boolean into an enum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that the patch changes only the final top-level targetlist, so lower plan nodes still compute the expensive expression and cost estimates do not reflect the saving. precedents_retrieved.title: Index Only Scan for index expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the planner so that index-only scans can be used when a query's target list or restriction clauses contain expressions that exactly match index expression columns, not only plain attribute columns. Matching requires the expression tree (or a subtree) to be identical to the index expression; no normalization of commutative or associative operators is attempted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Testing of the sixth patch version by Vladimir Sitnikov found an error ("variable not found in subplan target list") when queries access non-indexed columns alongside an expression index. Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback because these bugs precluded committing it before the CommitFest ended, while inviting resubmission and saying the effort was good.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix buffer pinning logic/visibility bugs in [SP-]Gist Index-Only Scans
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Geoghegan (pgeoghegan), Michail Nikolaev (nkey), Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a race in GiST and SP-GiST index-only scans, where concurrent VACUUM can remove a TID and set the visibility map bit before the scan checks it, so a dead tuple is returned. precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix ALTER TABLE DROP EXPRESSION with ONLY option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP EXPRESSION work on inheritance trees with more than one level, where it now fails with "must be applied to child tables too". It adds a `!recursing` check in ATPrepDropExpression() so the ONLY check runs only for the table named in the command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Peter Eisentraut asked why tablecmds.c passes recurse = false when recursing, and suggested a more consistent use of the two flags would make the existing code work. Tom Lane said that if the flags matter here, DROP EXPRESSION should not use ATSimpleRecursion. The author replied in December 2025 that v3 is correct, and no later reply appears before the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
Reverted commit(s): Don't allow GetTransactionSnapshot() in logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1585ff7387 changed GetTransactionSnapshot() to throw an error
if it's called during logical decoding, instead of returning the
historic snapshot. I made that change for extra protection, because a
historic snapshot can only be used to access catalog tables while
GetTransactionSnapshot() is usually called when you're executing
arbitrary queries. You might get very subtle visibility problems if
you tried to use the historic snapshot for arbitrary queries.

There's no built-in code in PostgreSQL that calls
GetTransactionSnapshot() during logical decoding, but it turns out
that the pglogical extension does just that, to evaluate row filter
expressions. You would get weird results if the row filter runs
arbitrary queries, but it is sane as long as you don't access any
non-catalog tables. Even though there are no checks to enforce that in
pglogical, a typical row filter expression does not access any tables
and works fine. Accessing tables marked with the user_catalog_table =
true option is also OK.

To fix pglogical with row filters, and any other extensions that might
do similar things, revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return a
historic snapshot during logical decoding.

To try to still catch the unsafe usage of historic snapshots, add
checks in heap_beginscan() and index_beginscan() to complain if you
try to use a historic snapshot to scan a non-catalog table. We're very
close to the version 18 release however, so add those new checks only
in master.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support SK_SEARCHNULL / SK_SEARCHNOTNULL for heap-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes heap scans honor SK_SEARCHNULL and SK_SEARCHNOTNULL scan keys in HeapKeyTest(), which skey.h documents as supported only for index scans. The goal was convenience for extensions that scan tables directly without SPI; a later follow-up by Jacob Champion added planner pushdown of IS [NOT] NULL quals into Seq Scan as scan keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas saw no benefit in heapam support alone and asked that nodeSeqScan.c use it, with performance results, and that the table AM API get an 'amsearchnulls' field. The author wanted to defer the executor part to a later patch, so Heikki marked the entry Returned with Feedback. The later executor and planner patches got no visible review before the entry closed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

roaster_notes.note: The precedent angle finds no fatal objection: the main reasons [P2] was returned are addressed in the series.

The series adds no SQL syntax, GUC or catalog object, so pg_dump round-trip and psql conventions are not affected. The EXPLAIN VERBOSE output changes, but it follows the existing practice for computed scan columns.

The series changes only planner and executor behaviour. It adds no on-disk format, no WAL record, no catalog column and no wire protocol message, so pg_upgrade, standbys and subscribers are not affected. Adding a NULL-default IndexAmRoutine callback and new plan node fields is a normal major-version ABI change. One persistent effect is minor and needs only a release-note item: 0001 changes <-> and ## results for points near a box edge, so existing expression indexes or stored generated columns built on those operators can hold old values after pg_upgrade until they are reindexed or recomputed. For the same reason 0001 should not be backpatched.

No security objection. The series changes no privilege check and adds no new object, role or setting, and it lets no one see data they could not already select. The substituted value is the result of an immutable index expression or ordering operator for a row that already passed every qual. The planner memory growth at deep joins is bounded by query size, like ordinary join search.
Patches 0001 to 0003 look separable and lower-risk. The objections concern mostly 0007 and 0008 and the long-term API.

For 0002-0004, the reuse of non-rechecked kNN ORDER BY values, no existing core feature does this. The only extension workaround, a backend global, breaks with nested ordering scans (message #9), so this angle raises nothing there.

Demand for the base change (0001-0003) is shown and has lasted: earlier threads, Matthias in message #3 and Oleg's ranked GIN test in message #16. The one objection covers only the planner extensions in 0007-0008.
